note: Context and On Earth cards. Every sentence restates the NASA Space Apps 2026 Flame in Freefall challenge description; no other source is used.

context.title: Apollo 1, 1967
context.text: The crew died in a pre-launch test when fire erupted in their oxygen-filled spacecraft. This is why the flammability of cabin materials is tested.

context.title: Mir space station
context.text: A multinational crew survived a fire caused by an oxygen generator failure. This is why detection and suppression matter.

context.title: Moon base atmosphere
context.text: A Moon base and pressurized rovers are expected to run at 30 % oxygen or more and 10.2 psi or less, to shorten pre-breathing for lunar excursions. That is more than a 40 % increase in oxygen concentration over Earth's air, making materials much more flammable.

earth.title: Fine-water-mist extinguishers
earth.text: According to the challenge description, fine-water-mist extinguishers developed for use on the ISS have practical applications on Earth.
earth.related_label: Fire suppression in this map: FLEX and FLEX-2

earth.title: Smoke detection
earth.text: According to the challenge description, NASA technology has led to improvements in smoke detection on Earth.
earth.related_label: Catalogued here: SAME, SAME-R and DAFT (not on the map)

earth.title: Firefighter gear
earth.text: According to the challenge description, NASA technology has also improved firefighter gear, including protective clothing and air tanks.
